thread:
Maria: Heads-up: dashboards showing EU aggregate-hours drift for 2026-03-19 02:00-05:00 UTC. ~2% of active tenants affected. We have the raw events in s3.
Jon: Are these late Kafka batches or an ingest schema hiccup?
Sasha: Late Kafka batches. Partition 13 had a GC pause around 02:00 and a bunch of events landed in s3 but never made it into the agg pipeline.
Maria: We need a targeted rehydrate. Two paths: console 'operator flow' (manual selection) or call recompute API and let the controller schedule it. Pros/cons?
Leo: API-first wins for reproducibility and audit trails. Console is convenient but opaque about job metadata.
Devon: Current API surfaces: POST /v1/recompute (sync/operator) and POST /v1/recompute/async which enqueues a job with dedupe_token + lane hints.
Maria: UX ask: console wants a cost + ETA preview before creating a job. Can /async expose a dryrun that the console can call?
Sasha: Planner already samples to estimate token counts and rows. The sampling error is typically 5-8% but fine for UI preview.
Jon: Routing worry: if many tenants rehydrate at once they flood low-priority lanes and starve other backfills. We need policy-aware ETA.
Leo: Policy-db can compute per-lane ETA given current backfill occupancy. We don't expose that to the console yet.
Devon: Proposal: add POST /v1/recompute/dryrun {tenant, windows, sample:true} that returns {estimated_rows, est_tokens, est_usd, recommended_lane, lane_eta_seconds, split_suggestion}
Maria: Example payload:
```json
POST /v1/recompute/dryrun
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-inc",
  "windows": ["2026-03-19T02:00:00Z/2026-03-19T05:00:00Z"],
  "sample": true
}
```
Jon: 'recommended_lane' should include fallback advice, e.g., "if est_tokens > 50M -> split by hour".
Leo: Also return policy metadata like per-tenant cap hits so console can warn operators.
Devon: Implementation notes: dryrun must not create leases or allocate slots. It should be a purely read-only planner + policy query. Console will generate a dedupe_token UUID when the operator confirms.
Maria: Important: tag origin=console in job.metadata and persist operator id for audit. Console should surface the generated dedupe_token post-submit.
Jon: Billing semantics question: should these rehydrates count against a tenant's reserved quota or a maintenance bucket? Customers expect internal ops fixes to not consume their quota.
Sasha: Historically we had 'maintenance' class for operator-driven small fixes. API-triggered jobs currently bill by default to tenant. We need a mapping and RBAC to allow overrides.
Leo: Solution: job.metadata.billing_class = maintenance|tenant. Default for console-originated operator flows -> maintenance. Allow override only for users with role 'backfill-admin'. UI should show a confirm if overriding to tenant billing.
Devon: Security: controller must enforce billing_class can't be spoofed by arbitrary callers. Only trusted auth tokens / roles can set maintenance.
Maria: Runbook draft:
- Run dryrun
- Review est_cost_usd + recommended_lane + lane_eta
- If lane_eta > 12h or est_tokens too large, split windows hourly
- Generate dedupe_token and submit with origin=console and operator id
- Watch /dash/telemetry/backfill-progress for 30m
Jon: Can we get an early-failure guard? If first slice produces row-count mismatch beyond threshold, auto-cancel remaining slices and open incident channel.
Sasha: Controller can emit slice-level checkpoints. Auto-cancel is doable but dangerous; make it a configurable threshold with default off. We should surface an operator opt-in flag.
Leo: For this incident let's do a small-slice API-run to validate the flow. I'll add /policy/estimate endpoint to return lane ETA and occupancy warnings (ETA: EOD).
Devon: I'll add dedupe_token visibility in controller logs + origin tags and a link back to console job UI (ETA: tomorrow).
Maria: I'll wire console dryrun + UI preview and add a confirmation modal that shows billing_class implications (ETA: tomorrow).
Sasha: I'll patch policy-db to return occupancy and a warn flag if global backfill concurrency > 80% (canary deploy scheduled).
Jon: I'll run a 1-hour slice for acme-inc after policy patch and report results here. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Deploy note: policy-db patch scheduled to canary at 2026-03-20T20:00Z.
Maria: Thanks. Action items:
- Leo: /policy/estimate (returns lane ETA + occupancy warnings) — EOD
- Devon: controller logging + dedupe_token surfacing + console link — tomorrow
- Maria: console dryrun wiring + cost preview + confirm UI — tomorrow
- Sasha: policy-db warn flag + slot telemetry — EOD
- Jon: run initial 1-hour API slice and monitor — after EOD
Jon: Will run and post progress here.
Maria: We'll reconvene after the first slice. Thanks everyone.
